design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (membership_charges_and_cancellations)

1. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[4, 4, 5, 6]. Nothing was occupied before this task (it is the first). This task claims membership_ext_term_charge_refund (4 factors, user tool confirm_annual_term_early_end_0b7355fe), membership_ext_carried_value_refund (4 factors, refund_carried_term_value_822a3886), membership_ext_move_to_monthly_charge (5 factors, move_annual_plan_to_monthly_dc3bc730) and membership_ext_pause_length (6 factors, book_membership_pause_b6aef13b). Left for task 1 (draw: 1 prerequisite, [4, 6]): the past-due settlement (renewal_retry capture, user) and the upgrade to Cartwise+ Annual (plan_switch capture) — a disjoint pair on a different member situation (past due, Student Monthly). Not claimed by anyone: leaving refunds, duplicate refunds (always the whole second capture, no factor can bear weight), early resume, cancellation and auto-renew (no number to compute).

2. Why this is a good test. The member asks only for the longest pause. Cartwise+ Annual cannot be paused (pause_allowed false), and the published route runs through three other writes: the member confirms the early end of the annual term (term-opening refund, her own write), the value carried from the last monthly charge is refunded, the membership moves to Cartwise+ Monthly with a charge worked out from the value still held, and only then is the pause length fixed. Every step is a multi-factor calculation over the membership ledger, the order ledger (member fee waivers, item charges) and the rewards tier; none is a lookup.

3. Problem tree (root membership_ext_pause_length).
 - pause <- move charge: value_input, gate plan_allowance, state form. Sentence (in the pause rule): "The pause length for a member who asked for a pause while on Cartwise+ Annual is not fixed until the membership shows Cartwise+ Monthly as its plan, with a plan-switch charge captured on the day its current period began." Only the move writes a plan of Cartwise+ Monthly with a same-day plan-switch charge (the task-1 upgrade writes an annual plan). False at the opening: memberships.variant_name = Cartwise+ Annual, current_period_start 2026-07-10.
 - move charge <- term-opening refund: value_input, gate value_held, state form. Sentence: "The move-to-monthly charge is fixed only after the charge that opened the annual term carries a prorated-annual refund booked against it." Only the term-opening refund writes a refund against the opening charge. False at the opening: no refund entry exists.
 - move charge <- carried-value refund: value_input, gate value_held, state form. Sentence: "The move-to-monthly charge is not fixed until the fee charge captured most recently before the annual term began carries its own refund of the value it carried into the term." Only the carried-value refund writes a refund against that earlier charge. False at the opening.
 Four-point test: each sentence joins this policy's own result to a record-visible state with an ordering connective ("only after", "not ... until", "not fixed until"), names no tool, id or snake_case token, and states exactly the scope of the edge. Directions are mixed (one affirmative, two negated). Topological order: term refund, carried refund, move, pause. The two refunds commute (order_uniqueness). Three value_input edges (>= 2 required).
 Deletion sensitivity (replay): skip the move -> pause 22 instead of 97; skip the term refund -> move charge 0.00 instead of 0.44; skip the carried refund -> move charge 0.00.

4. Factor cards (tier taken; baseline figure from the sensitivity run).
 Term-opening refund = 68.40 (all baselines 44.66): unused_share_method (method, multi-source, cross-difficulty order) enrolled 20 months AND 4 member fee waivers in the last month -> days 289/365 (64.50); opening_retention_rate (parameter) 2 months completed AND no retry capture in twelve months -> 1.00 (61.01); waiver_offset_window (parameter, order) 10 captures in twelve months -> last month's waivers 10.99 (64.73; near-miss: the 2025-08-28 capture is outside the twelve months and makes the count exactly 10); waiver_offset_rate (parameter, rewards) Gold -> 0.5 (62.91).
 Carried-value refund = 4.56 (all baselines 0.00): carried_share_method (method) switch 2 months ago AND carried 5.66 < 6.00 -> whole value (3.38); carried_retention_rate (parameter, rewards) Gold -> 1.00 (3.99); carried_handling_amount (parameter) no retry capture -> 0.00 (4.06); carried_waiver_share (parameter) 10 captures -> 0.10 of 10.99 (0.16).
 Move charge = 0.44 (all baselines 7.28): term_run_value_method (method) enrolled 20 months AND switch into the term 2 months ago (< 3) -> whole weeks 70 days (2.06); move_credit_share (parameter) no retry -> 1.00 (3.97); move_rate (parameter, rewards) Gold -> 0.90 (1.44); welcome_back_amount (parameter) 16 renewals -> 1.00 (1.44); activity_credit (parameter, order) 4 waivers in the last month -> 0.50 (0.94).
 Pause length = 97 (all baselines 90): tenure_extension (parameter, multi-source) 19 captures AND 20 months -> +28 (69); rewards_extension (parameter, rewards) Gold -> +10 (87); spending_extension (parameter, order) 235.46 in three months -> +7 (90; near-miss: the 2026-06-20 order is outside the window); earlier_pause_reduction (method: whole booked length vs a flat pause_min_days per earlier pause vs none) 30-day pause of 2026-01-28 -> -30 (127); fresh_period_reduction (parameter: share 1 / one half / 0) switch today AND charge 0.44 < 9.99 -> -15 (112); notice_extension (parameter) 30 days -> +7 (90).
 Every factor's tier rests on seeded rows (ledger counts, dates, order_events, rewards_accounts); no stamp field is read.

5. Base-invariant card. Refunds (subject membership_fee_refunded, membership_evt_fee_refund): the full-refund time gate is retired by a declared overwrite (the early-end refunds apply whenever asked); one_refund_per_charge holds (no refund exists against either charge). The carried-value refund also overrides "A refund of a first period or renewal charge ends the membership" (declared). Move (membership_plan_switched, membership_evt_plan_switch): switch_from_active holds (active; Cartwise+ Monthly is in Cartwise+ Annual's allowed targets); the next-renewal downgrade timing and the one-switch-per-period sentence are overridden by declaration. Pause (membership_paused, membership_evt_pause): pause_from_active and pause_cutoff hold after the move (active, Monthly allows pauses; last day to ask 2026-10-23, today 2026-09-24); the pause length range is overridden by declaration.

6. Business-object card. Target: membership 5634ee01-8268-4a30-8db6-6b8df776620e. Refund objects: the plan_switch charge of 2026-07-10 (term-opening refund) and the 2026-06-27 renewal (carried-value refund), each named by source_event_id. Rows entering aggregates: all fee charges on the membership (counts), the pause entry of 2026-01-28, the member fee waivers and item charges of the five orders (the 2026-06-20 order is excluded by every three-month window).

7. Persona. Renata volunteers the pause request and that she moved to the yearly plan in July (true: plan_switched_date 2026-07-10). Phone and email on request (verification needs 2 matches); DOB/ZIP only if asked. She reacts only after the agent explains other steps, runs the handed-over confirmation with the values given, never states or guesses a number, and closes when told the pause is booked. No extra asks.

8. Standard solution. Locate (phone) -> verify (phone + email) -> read membership, its ledger, orders, order ledger, rewards account -> hand over and have the member confirm the term-opening refund 68.40 against the opening charge -> book the carried refund 4.56 against the 2026-06-27 renewal -> move to Cartwise+ Monthly with charge 0.44 -> book the 97-day pause (2026-10-24 to 2027-01-28). Values were recomputed by check_compute on the handling-time world (initial_state plus earlier gold writes) and equal the gold arguments.

9. Draft recomputation from the visible context. Reading only the published rules, the tool schemas and the rows the finders return, the chain above is the only one: the pause rule names the Monthly state it waits on; only the move policy produces it; the move rule names the two refund states; the two refund rules say which charge each is booked against. No second equally correct write set exists (the refunds carry their own source charge; the move has no free parameter; the pause takes the computed length).

10. Revision 2 (policy-task audit rework; every item closed in the charter or the seed, numbers re-derived by replaying the real tools):
 - F1/F3: the move rule now covers only "a member on Cartwise+ Annual whose current annual term was opened by a plan switch from a monthly plan" (the only terms the carried-value refund can serve), and the term-opening refund likewise only terms "that a plan switch from a monthly plan opened"; term_run_value_method now splits on the age of the plan switch into the term (fewer than 3 months vs 3 or more), both tiers reachable. This world: switch 2026-07-10, 2 months -> whole weeks (unchanged method).
 - F2/O5: both refund policies now declare the base full_unused sentence superseded; the carried refund also declares "Monthly plans receive no refund outside the full-refund rule".
 - F4: earlier_pause_reduction is a genuine method (whole booked days vs a flat pause_min_days per earlier pause vs none); fresh_period_reduction relabelled parameter.
 - Order seed (audit finding 3): member service fees now follow order_evt_service_fee (member 5% bounded by the 3.00 floor, non-member 7.5%), and each difference is booked as an order_fee_waived row with waiver_basis member_service_fee_rate (1.66 on 2026-09-14, 1.35 on 08-29, 1.37 on 07-02, 0.86 on 06-20; the No-Rush order has none because both rates are 5%). Last-month member fee waivers are now 4 rows / 10.99, three-month 18.34. New values: term refund 68.40, carried refund 4.56, move charge 0.44, pause 97.
 - O1: move and upgrade declare the fee_billing "billed ... at the plan's period_fee_usd" clause superseded (membership_evt_fee_billing added to base_policy_refs).
 - O3: the move<-term condition names the charge whose billing_period_start equals current_period_start. O6: tool docstrings drop "afterwards"/"then". O7: waiver_offset_window relabelled parameter (the term refund keeps unused_share_method as its method). O2: moot (the term refund now only serves plan-switch-opened terms). O8: kept (the order-reading factors satisfy the cross-difficulty floor).
user_scenario:
You are Renata Castellanos, a 42-year-old physical therapist in Seattle who orders most of her groceries through Cartwise. You are calling because you are going to Tucson to look after your mother after her hip surgery; you leave in late October and do not expect to be back until well into the new year. You want your Cartwise+ membership paused while you are away, for as long as Cartwise will let you pause it. You say this plainly at the start: "I'll be away from late October into the new year, and I'd like to pause my Cartwise+ membership for as long as I'm allowed." You mention that you moved to the yearly plan back in July. You have no preference about exact dates beyond "as long as you can give me", and you want it done on this call.

You are warm but a little rushed, and you keep your answers short. You do not know how pauses, refunds or plan rules work at Cartwise and you do not guess at them. When the agent asks who you are, you give your mobile number, 2065510417. If they need a second detail, you give your email, renata.castellanos@brightmail.com. Only if they ask for more do you give your date of birth, 1984-06-19, or your home ZIP code, 98118.

Only after the agent has explained to you that other things must be done on your membership before the pause can be booked do you respond to them: you listen, say it sounds fine as long as you end up paused, and tell them to go ahead with whatever they need to do on their side. If the agent says that part of it is something only you can confirm and gives you an action with the exact values to use, you carry it out exactly as given, without changing anything, and tell them it went through. You do not know any of the amounts yourself; if the agent asks you what you expect back or what you think a charge should be, you say you have no idea and trust them to follow the rules. If the agent asks whether you want a different length than the longest one allowed, you say no, the longest one is what you want.

Once the agent tells you the pause is booked and gives you the dates, you thank them, say that is all you needed, and end the call.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The cutoff is counted in calendar days backward from current_period_end, so the last day to ask is current_period_end minus pause_request_cutoff_days, inclusive.

edges.condition: memberships.variant_name is Cartwise+ Monthly and a membership_fee_charged row with fee_type plan_switch and billing_period_start equal to memberships.current_period_start stands on the membership.
edges.policy_source: The pause length for a member who asked for a pause while on Cartwise+ Annual is not fixed until the membership shows Cartwise+ Monthly as its plan, with a plan-switch charge captured on the day its current period began.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At the opening the membership is on Cartwise+ Annual and its current period was opened on 2026-07-10 by the Monthly-to-Annual switch, not by a switch onto Cartwise+ Monthly.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The move writes variant_name Cartwise+ Monthly, current_period_start 2026-09-24, current_period_end 2026-10-24 and a plan_switch charge of 0.44 with billing_period_start 2026-09-24; the pause allowance then reads pause_max_days 90 and the fresh-period reduction of 15 days.

edges.condition: A membership_events row of type membership_fee_refunded with refund_type prorated_annual whose source_event_id is the fee charge whose billing_period_start equals memberships.current_period_start (the charge that opened the current annual term) stands on the membership.
edges.policy_source: The move-to-monthly charge is fixed only after the charge that opened the annual term carries a prorated-annual refund booked against it.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two refunds are parallel prerequisites of the move charge. Neither reads what the other writes: the term-opening refund reads the opening charge, the enrollment date, fee-charge and retry-capture counts, the term dates, order waivers and the rewards tier; the carried-value refund reads the plan fee, the opening charge, the switch date, retry-capture and fee-charge counts, order waivers and the rewards tier; refund entries enter neither computation. Run in either order the scratch replay gives 68.40 and 4.56 and the same terminal rows (each refund row id is derived from its own arguments), so both orders leave one terminal state. The move and the pause are strictly ordered by the two prerequisite sentences.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the move the membership stays on Cartwise+ Annual: pause_max_days reads 0, the fresh-period reduction is 0 and the notice window is 289 days, so pause_days would be 22 instead of 97 (and the plan_switch charge row and the Monthly plan would be missing from the terminal state).
Without the term-opening refund the value held stays 94.44, the value ahead exceeds the monthly fee and the move charge floors at 0.00 instead of 0.44.
Without the carried-value refund the value held is 30.60, the value ahead 11.61 and the move charge floors at 0.00 instead of 0.44.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for the longest pause and says she moved to the yearly plan in July (a fact of the membership record). It never mentions monthly billing, refunds, the opening charge, the carried value or any plan change as something to do; it reacts only after the agent explains that other things must be done before the pause, and runs the handed-over action with the values the agent gives. No policy id appears in it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: book_membership_pause_b6aef13b writes the pause whatever the plan or status; move_annual_plan_to_monthly_dc3bc730 switches and captures without looking for refunds; the two refund tools book their entry without checking dates, windows or earlier refunds. None of the four functions reads another entry to decide whether to act, raises or returns an error.
